title: GovDash becomes the AI infrastructure layer for GovCon
summary: Sean, Gavin, and Lauren talk about what GovDash as infrastructure that allows your team to fully leverage AI for GovCon workflows.
body_markdown:
**GovDash becomes the AI infrastructure layer for GovCon**


GovDash is easy to use out of the box, but increasingly built to function like infrastructure. Teams can configure workspaces, workflows, Agents, Skills, Memory, tools, and integrations around the way their business actually operates.


GovDash as infrastructure changes what is possible. Building an AI system that understands your company, connects to your existing stack, follows your processes, and can actually do work would normally require significant engineering, time, and money. GovDash gives government contractors that foundation out of the box, so they can shape it around their business in days rather than spending years building it themselves.


The result is a much more practical path to realizing the promise of AI: not another generic tool your team has to adapt to, but an AI operating system that adapts to your company.


## **Dash shifts from assistant to teammate**


> “Six months ago, Dash was very much an assistant. Dash is now doing the work for you. You go in, delegate work to Dash, and it’s able to understand your business, your strategy, and your internal knowledge, and take action for you.” - Gavin Kline, Head of Engineering


An assistant waits for a prompt and produces a draft. A teammate takes an assignment, does the work, and comes back with something ready for review.


That kind of delegation only works when the system understands your business well enough to act without being walked through every step. That is what much of the infrastructure underneath GovDash is designed to enable.


## **Institutional knowledge is the foundation**


Every GovCon company has more information than its people can reasonably keep track of. Past performance buried in SharePoint. Six versions of the same labor rate sheet. Win themes from bids the team barely remembers. Capture notes sitting in someone’s inbox.


That institutional knowledge is one of the most valuable assets a contractor has. The problem is usually finding it, organizing it, and putting it to work when it matters.


> “With a company’s institutional knowledge and their data, we’re able to be more specific with the things we’re outputting, and we know that it’s going to take less work for them to verify everything, because it’s already starting from their tribal knowledge.” - Gavin Kline


GovDash structures that information into a common data layer, then gives teams several ways to put it to work.


## **Memory, Skills, and Connectors**


**Memory** holds preferences and context so you don’t have to keep re-explaining yourself. GovDash learns how you work and uses that context across future work. As your team uses the system, that context compounds rather than starting over with every pursuit.


**Skills** capture how your business does the work. Your bid and no-bid criteria. How you build a compliance matrix. How you interpret Sections L and M. The procedures your team has refined over years can be turned into repeatable processes that GovDash follows every time.


**Connectors** bring in the systems and information your team already uses. Email, calendars, messaging, document repositories, and other applications can connect directly to GovDash, giving Dash and your Agents the context and tools they need to get work done.


And GovDash doesn’t have to live in another tab. With Microsoft Teams and Slack bots, your team can talk to Dash, delegate work, and get results directly inside the communication tools where they already work. The goal is for Dash to operate less like software you log into and more like another member of the team.


This is where the infrastructure idea come into play. GovDash provides the underlying data, connections, tools, and agent infrastructure, while each company can configure the system around its own knowledge, processes, and people. What would otherwise require a large internal AI effort can be built around your business in a fraction of the time and cost.


## **Agents do the work**


Agents put that infrastructure to work.


> “Agents really unlock the autonomous workflow. Since Agents launched a few months ago, we’ve seen over 270% month-over-month growth in Agent runs.” - Sean Doherty, CEO


Agents can work across every GovDash Module, from capture through contract, with access to your Memory, Skills, connected systems, and GovDash tools. Describe what you want accomplished and Dash can configure an Agent to do it, and awaits your approval before taking any action.


Instead of spending hours gathering data, updating fields, drafting emails, or running repetitive research, teams can delegate that work and spend more time making pursuit decisions and talking to customers. For example, you may set up an Agent that goes through Outlook to find any information in emails that may be relevant to opportunities in your pipeline, and automatically create notes for your team to review.


Agents like this are already producing meaningful returns. Cape Fox FCG runs BD for 12 federal subsidiaries on GovDash. Its team uses Agents to compile the competitive landscape as soon as an opportunity enters the pipeline, saving three to four hours each time. The company increased output last year without adding headcount.


## **You still make the calls**


More autonomy makes human oversight more important, not less.


> “Especially in an area as compliance-sensitive as the government contracting world, we’ve built our Agents to keep that human in the loop as one of our core values. When someone’s submitting a piece of work, Dash is always going to ask for approval to make sure that it meets the company’s expectations and we’re putting out good results.” - Gavin Kline, Head of Engineering


Teams control what Agents can do, approvals can be required before consequential actions, and Agent activity is auditable. GovDash can do more of the work without taking control away from the people responsible for the outcome.


## **Flexible pricing for teams of all sizes**


As GovDash has become more configurable, we’ve changed our pricing so teams can adopt it the same way.


Teams can now subscribe to individual Modules instead of buying the entire platform at once. If your capture team is ready for GovDash but your proposal team isn’t, start with Capture and add Proposal later. A Module subscription includes everything in that area, including user-initiated workflows and Dash, while Agents run at a 25% discount in subscribed Modules.


We’re also introducing **Credits** , a shared currency for Agents and work performed in Modules you haven’t subscribed to. Teams get one workspace balance, real-time usage visibility, and controls over spending.


For smaller teams, or companies just entering government contracting, we’ve also introduced a credit-only option. You can start using GovDash without committing to a Module, then add subscriptions as your usage grows.


The idea is simple: start where the value is highest, configure GovDash around the way your company works, and expand from there.


And for small teams or those just entering the government contracting space, we have introduced a credit-only plan to explore GovDash before committing to a Module.[Book a demo](https://www.govdash.com/book-a-demo) to map the best Modules for your workflows and test GovDash on a live solicitation today.
